# SecureStore

> One secure-credential API for Swift on Apple platforms, Windows, Linux, and Android. Five
> operations over the OS secure store — set, read, remove, removeAll, and prefix-scoped key
> enumeration — backed by Keychain Services on Apple, Credential Manager on Windows, the
> Secret Service on Linux, and a host-registered C bridge on Android, so shared Swift business
> logic can store tokens on any of them without a Java-interop layer.

Swift 6.3+, SPM package with one library: `SecureStore`.

## Reference

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlexNachbaur/securestore-swift/main/README.md): overview, installation, usage, Android registration
- [Host bridge ABI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlexNachbaur/securestore-swift/main/docs/design/host-bridge-abi.md): the C contract, ownership rules, status codes, and host obligations
- [API documentation](https://swiftpackageindex.com/AlexNachbaur/securestore-swift/documentation): DocC
- [CHANGELOG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlexNachbaur/securestore-swift/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Key facts

- `SecureStore` is a protocol with one backend type per platform, chosen at compile time:
  `KeychainSecureStore` (`#if canImport(Security)`), `WindowsSecureStore` (`#if os(Windows)`),
  `LinuxSecureStore` (`#if os(Linux)`, needs libsecret at build time and a Secret Service
  provider at run time), and `HostSecureStore` everywhere else (Android). There is no runtime
  fallback between them. `PlatformSecureStore` is a typealias for whichever one the current
  platform compiles, so shared code can write `PlatformSecureStore(service:)` without `#if`.
- The operations are `set(_:for:)`, `data(for:)`, `remove(_:)`, `removeAll()`, and
  `keys(withPrefix:)`; `allKeys()` is the empty-prefix convenience. All are synchronous and can
  block (a Linux keyring may prompt to unlock) — call them off the main thread.
- **Every operation throws, including reads.** A missing item is `nil`; anything else throws. Do
  not suggest wrappers that collapse failures into `nil` — separating "absent" from "unreadable"
  is a deliberate design property, not an oversight.
- **There is no `accessGroup`.** Sharing scope is an opaque `namespace: String?`. On Apple it maps
  to a keychain access group; hosts without an equivalent ignore it. **On macOS it is ignored
  unless the store is created with `KeychainSecureStore(…, usesDataProtectionKeychain: true)`**,
  which requires a keychain entitlement (unsigned processes get `errSecMissingEntitlement`). Do not add Apple-specific
  parameters to the cross-platform API.
- On Android the host must call `securestore_register_host` (typically from
  `Application.onCreate`) before any store is used; until then operations throw
  `SecureStoreError.backendNotRegistered` rather than silently no-op'ing.
- The C ABI never transfers pointer ownership: results come back through sink callbacks that copy
  within the call, and every operation returns an `Int32` status (`0` ok, `1` not found).

## Contributing

- [CONTRIBUTING](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlexNachbaur/securestore-swift/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): setup, style, and what a good change looks like
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlexNachbaur/securestore-swift/main/AGENTS.md): instructions for agents working in the repository itself
- Behavioural changes belong in the backend-agnostic contract suite, which runs against every
  backend so they cannot drift.
